items.what: The agreement exists or the cash was paid. Still read the amount: a ceiling is not always disbursed.
items.why: FedForge uses FINAL when a notice says the deal is signed, awarded, or paid — the strongest status weight on the ranked screen.

items.what: A loan or award that still depends on conditions, milestones, or closing documents.
items.why: Large Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) and Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) rows are CONDITIONAL — they are not cash out the door.

items.what: A non-binding or pre-definitive signal that an agency intends to fund something.
items.why: The Jul 29 CHIPS R&D package is tagged LOI. GlobalFoundries (GFS) is the only verified ticker in that package.

items.what: A DoD/DoW contract vehicle that lets work start before all terms are negotiated. The ceiling (face) is not the same as obligated cash.
items.why: THAAD, PAC-3, and AMRAAM cards show obligated vs face. Rank weights obligated cash far above the UCA ceiling.

items.what: The cabinet department that runs nuclear energy, loans, and many science programs.
items.why: HALEU, Civil Nuclear Credit, and EDF loans are DOE notices.

items.full: Department of Defense / Department of War
items.what: The U.S. military department. 2026 notices on war.gov use Department of War; older sources say DoD.
items.why: Lockheed and RTX interceptor and munitions notices are DoW/DoD contract announcements.

items.full: National Institute of Standards and Technology
items.what: Commerce Department lab that also houses the CHIPS program office.
items.why: CHIPS definitive agreements and letters of intent are NIST/Commerce notices.

items.what: The DoD/DoW agency that buys missile-defense systems.
items.why: The THAAD undefinitized contract action is an MDA notice.

items.what: A DoD/DoW office that uses credit tools (loans, not just grants) for dual-use supply chains.
items.why: Niron and Sila rows are OSC conditional loan commitments — private recipients.

items.what: The DOE semi-autonomous agency for the nuclear weapons enterprise and nonproliferation.
items.why: Some university nuclear primes and lab work sit under NNSA even when the public card says DOE.

items.what: Commerce bureau that runs export controls and some Defense Production Act allocation rules.
items.why: Black-mass / tungsten scrap rules on the pipeline page are BIS, not a company grant.

items.full: Export-Import Bank of the United States
items.what: The U.S. export credit agency. It finances U.S. exports, not a typical procurement award.
items.why: Named when export-credit tools show up next to industrial policy; FedForge still requires a sourced dollar to list a company.

items.full: Creating Helpful Incentives to Produce Semiconductors
items.what: The 2022 statute (and follow-on program) that funds U.S. semiconductor manufacturing and R&D.
items.why: USA Rare Earth, SandboxAQ, I-Pulse, Bosch, and the GFS letter of intent are CHIPS notices.

items.what: A DOE program that pays to keep at-risk U.S. nuclear plants operating.
items.why: PG&E's $271M Diablo Canyon payment is the first CNC disbursement in this window.

items.what: The DOE loan/financing label used on the $17.5B AP1000 conditional package in this window.
items.why: That row is CONDITIONAL and the named recipient is private (Westinghouse sponsor).

items.full: Definitive funding agreement / direct funding agreement
items.what: The closed CHIPS award document — stronger than a letter of intent.
items.why: USAR, SandboxAQ, I-Pulse, and Bosch cards are DFAs. GFS is still an LOI, not a DFA.

items.what: The statute that lets the President prioritize domestic production of critical items.
items.why: The recoverable-minerals determination on the pipeline page is DPA policy, not an award to a ticker.

items.what: A set-aside program for small U.S. businesses to do federal R&D.
items.why: Many new-prime rows are SBIR Phase I/II — not megadeals, and usually no public ticker.

items.what: Like SBIR, but requires a research-institution partner.
items.why: DOE ROCKS and NSF rows tagged SBIR/STTR on the new-primes strip.

items.what: U.S. government-facilitated sales of U.S. defense articles to partner nations.
items.why: The AMRAAM UCA obligated figure is FMS money — still federal, still not a stock forecast.

items.what: A nuclear reactor design meant to be factory-built in smaller units than a conventional plant.
items.why: FedForge's nuclear lane includes SMRs, fuel, and existing plants — Oklo on the roster is previously reported, not an in-window prime.

items.what: Uranium enriched above typical power-reactor levels but below weapons-grade, used by many advanced reactors.
items.why: Centrus / American Centrifuge Operating holds the DOE HALEU commercial-capacity task order (ticker LEU).

items.what: A Generation III+ large pressurized-water reactor design.
items.why: The $17.5B DOE EDF conditional loans are for AP1000 long-lead items. Private sponsor — not on the ranked public list.

items.what: Seventeen metallic elements used in magnets, electronics, and defense systems.
items.why: USA Rare Earth and several university/SBIR new primes are REE or magnet-material work.

items.what: A wide-bandgap semiconductor material used in power electronics.
items.why: I-Pulse and Bosch CHIPS DFAs, plus an Arkansas university SiC CMOS prime, sit in this lane.

items.what: A Lockheed Martin missile-defense interceptor system.
items.why: The Jun 24 MDA undefinitized contract action is THAAD — read $842.9M obligated vs $35.33B face.

items.what: A Lockheed Martin hit-to-kill interceptor for the Patriot air-defense system. MSE means Missile Segment Enhancement.
items.why: The Jul 30 Army modification is PAC-3 MSE. $0 was obligated on that mod. Face is not cash.

items.what: A Raytheon (RTX) air-to-air missile family.
items.why: The Jun 24 UCA is AMRAAM D4/C9. Obligated cash is the Foreign Military Sales slice, not the full ceiling.

items.what: A contract type where the price is set; the contractor bears cost overrun risk.
items.why: The Centrus HALEU task order is FFP at $900M ($1.07B with options).

items.what: The industry codes used to classify federal awards (for example semiconductor manufacturing 334413).
items.why: The USAspending snapshot was queried with nuclear, magnet, and semiconductor NAICS plus keywords.

items.what: The official public database of federal spending. Award Amount is what the API returned, not a FedForge judgment that funds are fully disbursed.
items.why: The 46 new primes are a static USAspending snapshot. The API does not send CORS headers, so the browser cannot refresh it.

items.what: The government-wide registry for entities that want to do business with the U.S. government.
items.why: Prime recipients on USAspending are SAM-registered entities. Registration is not a stock listing.
